US technology ETFs are seeing massive wave of deleveraging:

The 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, is down -90% from its June peak, to its lowest since September 2025.

This marks its 2nd-largest drawdown since the fund's inception in March 2010, surpassed only by the -91% decline during the 2022 bear market.

By comparison, the fund dropped -89% during the July 2024-April 2025 period.

Meanwhile, the 3x leveraged long Nasdaq 100 ETF, $TQQQ, is down -53% from its June peak to its lowest since early April.

Since October 5th alone, the fund has dropped -51%.

For perspective, $TQQQ fell -61% during the February-April 2025 drawdown.

Leveraged tech funds have experienced a historic liquidation wave.

The US equity market experienced just one of its sharpest sell-offs on record:

The S&P 500 fell -11.6% from its October 6th peak in just 33 trading days, placing the decline among the 15 fastest corrections since 1928.

By comparison, at the start of the 2022 bear market, it took 34 sessions for the index to fall at least -10%.

During the 2020 pandemic selloff, the same decline took just 6 trading days, while in March 2025 it took 17 sessions.

Overall, 4 of the 15 fastest corrections since 1928 have occurred over the last 6 years.

Meanwhile, 94% of S&P 500 stocks were down last week, with 111 declining by at least -10%.

At the same time, 11 stocks in the index were down by at least -20%.

Market sentiment has become extremely pessimistic.

BREAKING: The 10Y Note yield has traded above 5.00% for 27 trading days so far in 2026, the longest streak for any year since 2007.

Last week, the 10Y Note yield surged +29 basis points, moving back above 5.00% and marking its largest weekly increase since April 2025.

The 10Y is now on track for its longest period above 5.00% since 2006, when 65 trading days above this threshold were recorded.

Year-to-date, the 10Y Note yield is up +94 basis points, to 5.10%, after peaking at 5.36% in early October, its highest level since 2002.

This puts the yield on track for its 6th consecutive annual increase.

Prices of imported computers and semiconductors are skyrocketing:

US import prices for computers, peripherals, and semiconductors surged +26.5% YoY in October, their largest annual increase on record in data going back to the 1990s.

This also marks the 7th consecutive YoY increase of at least +10.0%.

MoM, the US Import Price Index for computers, peripherals, and semiconductors rose +3.6%, to 61.1 points, its highest level since December 2008.

Since March 2025, this figure has soared +30.0%, reversing its long-term downwtrend.

The AI investment boom is reversing decades of falling electronics prices.

China's economic slowdown is deepening:

China's retail sales rose just +0.4% YoY in October, the 3rd-lowest reading since December 2022, and well below the expected +0.8% growth.

This marks a sharp deceleration from a +1.1% YoY increase in September.

Retail sales are now on pace to end the year with their weakest growth since 2020.

Meanwhile, industrial production grew +4.8% YoY last month, down from +5.5% in September, and the slowest expansion in 3 months.

Furthermore, fixed-asset investment fell -8.1% YoY in the first 10 months of 2026, its biggest decline since the 2020 pandemic.

In October alone, investment dropped -16.9% YoY, the largest decline on record outside the pandemic.

China's domestic demand continues to deteriorate.

BREAKING: AI-related investment contributed +1.27 percentage points to real US GDP growth in Q1 through Q3 2026.

This represents ~65% of the economy's cumulative growth of ~2% over this period.

Software investment contributed the most, at +0.45 percentage points, followed by computers and peripheral equipment, at +0.37 percentage points.

Communication and electrical equipment contributed +0.21 percentage points, R&D +0.16 percentage points, and data center structures +0.07 percentage points.

AI investment has become the backbone of the US economy.

Anthropic is sitting on an enormous cash pile:

Anthropic's cash and cash equivalents are up to a record $237 billion following its IPO.

This comes as its IPO raised $81 billion, with another $26 billion secured through a private placement with selected investors.

By comparison, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, SpaceX, $SPCX, and Apple, $AAPL, each hold less than 25% of this amount.

Anthropic's cash pile is therefore larger than those 4 companies combined.

This is also 8 times Nvidia's, $NVDA, cash balance, 12 times Microsoft's, $MSFT, and 22 times Meta's, $META.

For perspective, Berkshire Hathaway’s cash pile stands at $377 billion.

Anthropic has a huge amount of cash to deploy.

Markets are a battle against your own psychology.

We live in a time of profound technological abundance, but your human brain is primed to recognize fear at every turn. Your very instincts mislead you.

What's happening with sentiment?

It's hard to remember a time with as much negativity as we are seeing now.

The world is in its biggest technological revolution in history, yet so many people want it to fail. Why?

AI has the potential to create a world of unprecedented abundance, and this should be a time for optimism.

Instead of focusing on the opportunities ahead, the conversation is dominated by fear, skepticism, and predictions of collapse.

Once again, the comments on this post will prove our point exactly.

Every major technological revolution in history has been met with skepticism, but progress has continued regardless.

The opportunities being created right now are generational.

Don't let short-term market sentiment blind you to long-term opportunity.

US semiconductor stocks are experiencing incredible volatility:

The Semiconductor Index to S&P 500 ratio is down to 1.45 points, its lowest since April 2026.

This ratio has declined -0.46 points, or -24%, from its mid-June peak.

Over this period, SOX has fallen -24%, while the S&P 500 has gained +2%.

The relative decline is comparable to the one seen following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst.

However, the ratio is still up +142% since the 2022 bear market low of, has also declined for 8 consecutive trading sessions, its longest streak since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

Semiconductor stocks are more volatile than ever.
